_doc: Higgs production cross sections at MH=125, in picobarns, assuming BR(H -> long-lived pair) = 1. Multiply by the branching ratio you are actually assuming.
_note: JMTucker multiplies xsec by filterEff at load time (Samples.py:113). Kamui keeps them separate so both are visible; the weight formula applies both.

WplusH.source: JMTucker Samples.py: 3*(9.541e-02), inclusive W+H 0.8502 times BR(W->lv), once per lepton flavour

WminusH.source: JMTucker Samples.py: 3*(5.981e-02), inclusive W-H 0.5328 times BR(W->lv), once per lepton flavour

ZH.source: JMTucker Samples.py: 3*(2.596e-02), qq-initiated ZH->llH, total ZH per flavour 2.996e-02 minus the gg component

ggZH.source: JMTucker Samples.py: 3*(3.995e-03), gg-initiated ZH->llH, inclusive ggZH 0.1184 times BR(Z->ll)

_filterEffNote: The ggH -> SS -> 4d samples carry a generator filter. The efficiency depends only on the scalar mass.

HToSSTo4d.source: JMTucker Tools/python/Samples.py, filter_eff on the ggHToSSTodddd samples

_weightFormula: N_expected = lumi[pb^-1] * xsec[pb] * filterEff / sumGenWeight * sum(per-event weights of passing events)
_weightNote: The denominator is the sum of generator weights over the whole sample, not the generated event count. JMTucker reads it from the h_sums histogram (mcStat/h_sums, else mfvWeight/h_sums) and computes xsec/sumw in Sample.partial_weight. Kamui ntuples carry genWeight per event, so the equivalent denominator is the sum of genWeight over every event produced, before any selection.
_filterEffScope: JMTucker multiplies xsec by filterEff for signals only (Samples.py:113). Background cross sections there are already the filtered, effective numbers. Kamui keeps xsec and filterEff separate for every process, so the formula above always applies both.
